I am 68 years old. I finished primary school and that was it. I have been working these fields since I was 18, so 50 years now. My father taught me, and I learned the rest by watching what works and what does not.

My farm is 8 mu. It is just me and my wife now. We have a well, so I can irrigate when I need to, but pumping water costs money, so I do not waste it. All 8 mu are wheat-maize rotation. I do not plant cotton anymore — too much labor, and the bugs are terrible.

**My wheat this year**

I will plant wheat in October, right after the maize comes off. First I run the rotary tiller. I know some people say no-till, but for wheat I have always tilled, and I am not changing now. Last year my wheat gave me about 1000 jin per mu, and I want the same.

For seed, I use what my neighbors use — improved varieties. I save some seed and buy some. I sow about 30 jin per mu.

For fertilizer, I put down one bag of compound fertilizer per mu before sowing — that is 50 kg. The bag says 15-15-15. Then in March, when the wheat turns green, I spread another bag of urea per mu, 50 kg. I know that is a lot, but last year the neighbor across the road used less and his wheat was thin. I would rather spend the money on fertilizer than risk a bad harvest. A bad harvest means disaster. Wasting some fertilizer is just money.

I irrigate three times: once after sowing if the soil is dry, once at jointing in spring, and once when the heads come out. The well pump runs on electricity, so each time costs me, but wheat needs water.

For chemicals, I spray herbicide once before sowing to kill the weeds. Then I spray for aphids and diseases twice in spring. Three times total.

**My maize this year**

After I harvest wheat in June, I plant maize the same day or the next. I do not till — I plant right into the wheat stubble. Everyone does it this way now. It saves time and the stubble keeps some moisture.

For seed, I buy Denghai 605 hybrid seed from the dealer. It costs more, but the yield is good. Last year I got about 1100 jin per mu. I plant about 3 jin of seed per mu.

For fertilizer, at planting I put one bag of compound fertilizer per mu — about 40 kg of the high-nitrogen kind, 30-5-5. Then at the big trumpet stage, I topdress with half a bag of urea, about 25 kg per mu. That gives the corn a push when it needs it.

I irrigate twice: once after sowing if it is dry, and once when the tassels come out. Summer usually brings some rain, so two times is enough.

For chemicals, I spray herbicide once after planting, and I spray for corn borers once. That is two times total.

I know fertilizer and seed prices have gone up. Last year compound fertilizer was around 120 yuan per bag and urea was 90. I have to watch my money. But cutting back on fertilizer is gambling with my food and my income. I will do what I did last year, maybe a tiny bit more, and hope the weather holds.
